newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS crudes extend technical weaknes late.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS crudes extend technical weaknes late.

text.p: U.S. crude futures eased in the ACCESS overnight market Wednesday after failing to break through key price levels during daytime trade, dealers said.
Crude oil for June delivery on NYMEX traded at $20.12 overnight, down nine cents a barrel from the daytime close, with traders saying the contract could move either up or down tomorrow.

"Long-term people are looking for (crude oil) rallies on the back of gasoline, but tomorrow it's hard to call," one trader said, speculating gasoline would reverse its loses on ACCESS and extend today's 55-cent-gallon-rise, lifting crude.
Others said crude would fall victim to more technical weakness on Thursday, after failing to break $20.53 today.
Meanwhile, unleaded gasoline for June eased after-hours to 62.30 cents a gallon, down 0.11 cents.
The May contract ended at the close of daytime trade.
After-hours, NYMEX June heating oil fell to 54.75 cents, down 0.17 cents as a sell-off ensued in a technical reaction to Tuesday's heavy buying.

Volumes were light Wednesday overnight, with about 305 crude lots traded in June, while heating oil saw 171 exchanged in the front month. June gasoline volume stood around 36 lots several hours into ACCESS.
